title: Consent-aware stream filter + quarantine and deferred erasure for console analytics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a consent-aware streaming filter that quarantines events containing possible PII or revoked-consent markers and enqueues deferred erasure jobs for eventual deletion. The service will sit as a consumer of the console analytics topic (Redpanda/Kafka) and apply lightweight, deterministic detectors (hash-based allowlist + regex heuristics + tokenized field rules) to route events into three paths: 1) passthrough (no PII), 2) quarantine (requires human/manual remediation or additional enrichment), 3) immediate erase (consent revoked and deterministic mapping to an identifiable token). Quarantined events are written to an immutable, access-restricted S3 bucket with object-level metadata capturing reason, detector version, partition/offset, and correlation id. Deferred erasure jobs will be enqueued to the eraser service which executes idempotent deletes against storage backends and emits attestation tokens for the audit ledger. The flow must preserve ordering for session-scoped events, expose high-cardinality metrics for backlog/backpressure, and provide a fast-fail path if downstream erasure systems are degraded.
acceptance_criteria: Stream filter deployed to staging consuming analytics topic with <5ms median filtering latency per event under 10k tps load
Detectors can be hot-swapped via config without consumer restart; detector versions recorded on quarantined objects
Quarantined events stored in access-controlled S3 prefix with server-side encryption and KMS key; objects include metadata tags for audit
Deferred erasure jobs produced to eraser queue are idempotent and include provenance (source topic, offset, detector-id)
End-to-end test shows revoked-consent event results in erasure attestation within SLA (configurable, default 24h) in 95% of cases
Monitoring dashboards for erasure_backlog, quarantine_inflow_rate, filter_rejection_rate, and avg_filter_latency exist and alert on SLO breaches
Canary rollout plan validated: 1% of traffic for 24h with real data; no increase in error budget or >5% increase in end-to-end latency

rollout_plan: Stage: Deploy to staging cluster, run synthetic + sampled production traffic for 72h
Canary: 1% production traffic for 24h, monitor latency & error budget
Ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks at each step and auto-rollback on threshold breach
Fallback: If S3 write latency causes backlog growth >2x baseline, automatically switch to pass-through mode and create incident SEV2
test_plan: Unit tests for detector rules and deterministic outcomes
Integration test that simulates revoked-consent flow through filter -> quarantine -> eraser -> attestation
Load test at 2x expected peak (20k tps) to validate CPU and IO profile
Chaos test: simulate temporary KMS outage and ensure no PII exfiltration; quarantine should be locked and jobs queued locally
E2E acceptance test with legal team verifying attestation artifact format
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Regex detectors cause CPU spikes at high QPS. Mitigation: sample-based heavy-rule execution, use compiled automata and JIT-friendly libraries
Risk: Quarantine S3 bucket becomes a single point for PII. Mitigation: strict IAM, KMS per-customer keys, automated export and purge policies, periodic manual review window
Risk: Ordering semantics broken for session-scoped erasure. Mitigation: partition-aware processing and per-session tombstone markers with idempotent delete semantics
Risk: Erasure backlog growth under downstream outage. Mitigation: backpressure signals to producer, circuit-breaker to swap to pass-through with incident alerting
